specs.label: S1
specs.name: lateral-hip-opening
specs.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand.
Asset type: one premium mobile fitness App icon concept for HipLab, a hip mobility and flexibility training app.
Create a single original, extremely simple sports symbol on a full-bleed square graphite background #101316. One centered, faceless abstract adult human figure, made of broad smooth curved strokes with blunt rounded ends and one small circular head. The movement must make the pelvis and opening/stretching of the hips visually clear. The style is a polished minimal brand mark, not a detailed exercise illustration.
Color and finish: jade green #3CCFA4 as the dominant body color, deep jade for subtly rounded edges, a very restrained warm ivory #F2F3F5 accent. Refined soft satin relief with slight physical thickness and controlled soft studio light; the icon's attractive tactile quality comes from the clean bevel and broad calm surfaces. No busy texture, no shiny toy plastic, no glass, no metallic chrome, no luminous aura.
Composition: straight-on frontal/near frontal, centered, balanced negative space, complete symbol within the middle 70 percent of the canvas and generous breathing room. Normal square outer corners. Make the silhouette immediately legible at 32px; large forms, at most 4 to 6 elements. No text, letters, numerals, labels, watermarks, grids, frames, decorative particles, props, dumbbells, skeletons, anatomical drawings or mascot face. Deliver one finished square image, not a presentation sheet.
Specific symbol: a clear side-lunge hip-opening stretch, like a very simplified Cossack stretch. The body is lowered into one deeply bent supporting leg while the opposite leg extends outward low to the side. A compact upright torso and one gently extended arm balance the pose. Use one generous continuous curved shape flowing from the torso through the pelvis into the bent thigh, plus a broad clean extended leg, rather than a complex stick figure. The opening between the thighs is broad and clearly expresses hip flexibility. A single short ivory crescent integrated at the hip crease emphasizes the hip articulation, not a floating anatomical marker. The overall gesture feels athletic, mobile and calm.
